 Colonel Family Connections offers child care support for Nicholls student-parents
 Leslie Rivero , Staff Writer 
 • 
 November 20, 2026 
 Students at Little Colonels Academy participate in Red-Out Friday. Photo via Little Colonels Academy, Nicholls State University 
 Balancing college coursework with the daily realities of raising a child brings serious financial and logistical pressure for student-parents.  
 To help ease that load, Nicholls is operating Colonel Family Connections, an early learning subsidy program built to make child care more affordable for eligible students working toward their degrees. 
 What is Colonel Family Connections? 
 Colonel Family Connections is Nicholls’s Child Care Access Means Parents in School, or CCAMPIS, early learning subsidy program.  
 Backed by a federal CCAMPIS grant, the program offers need-based assistance to help low-income, Pell-eligible student-parents cover child care tuition and related fees.  
 Depending on space availability, eligible families can access care through Little Colonels Academy on campus or the West Ascension Early Learning Center in Donaldsonville. 
 What Students Are Eligible? 
 To qualify for Colonel Family Connections, a student must be a Nicholls student-parent and hold legal guardianship over the child for whom assistance is requested.  
 Applicants also need to have a current FAFSA on file, meet the program’s Pell Grant eligibility standards and show a willingness to apply for other available child care aid, such as Louisiana’s CCAP program, when applicable. 
 Enrollment and academic standing rules apply as well. Undergraduate students must carry at least 12 credit hours, while graduate students must take at least nine credit hours if unemployed or six credit hours if employed.  
 Students must also meet academic requirements and maintain the minimum GPA required by their degree program to stay eligible over time. 
 How Might the Program Benefit Student-Parents? 
 For student-parents and students who hold legal guardianship over a child, high child care costs may make staying in school feel out of reach.  
 By helping pay for child care tuition and associated fees through need-based support, Colonel Family Connections offers support for low-income households. Having access to approved options like Little Colonels Academy on campus or the West Ascension Early Learning Center in Donaldsonville can also give families early learning support while students attend classes, study and finish their degrees. 
 How to Apply 
 Students planning to apply should gather their paperwork ahead of time, including a current FAFSA and financial aid award letter, proof of household income like recent pay stubs or tax documents, a birth certificate for each child needing assistance, household and child care provider information and any applicable CCAP records. 
 Applying involves two steps, starting with enrollment if a child is not already enrolled at Little Colonels Academy or the West Ascension Early Learning Center.  
 Those applying to Little Colonels Academy should note their intent to apply for CCAMPIS support in the Department section of the enrollment application. 
 Applicants also need to submit the online Student Parent CCAMPIS Subsidy Application. Applying does not guarantee a subsidy or a spot at a center, since awards depend on eligibility checks, available funding and provider openings.  
 Students with questions can reach out to [email protected] .
